title: Twenty-cell panels certified 60 and 65 percent of changed links in two passive adult worm models
abstract: We tested whether partial steady transfer measurements can locate one strengthened electrical link in passive models of two adult C. elegans maps. We used 180 common cells and 262 and 296 electrical links. A standard inverse update gives a unit response signature for each link. A nearest-signature distance above 0.10 certifies identity under an assumed processed-signature error at most 0.05. Across 50 random 20-cell panels, the mean certified shares were 59.98 and 64.76 percent. With 80 cells they were 91.98 and 91.97 percent. Full observation certified all links. Low and high leak assumptions gave different separation. Degree-ranked panels did not uniformly exceed random-panel means. Full inverses checked every link update, and explicit outer products independently checked selected panel counts. The error bound concerns normalized signatures, not raw voltage. Unknown conductance, incomplete electrical maps, a known-baseline assumption, and no measured activity limit use in living brains. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, hashes and external-data retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Mean certified link shares across random cell panels in two passive adult worm models. Bands show panel variation, not animal uncertainty.
